record.paper_title: Open Problems and Conjectures Related to the Theory of Mathematical Quasicrystals
record.original_question: Does the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel tiling have a nonzero absolutely continuous component?

evidence.quote: Problem 2.3.2 Does the diffraction measure of the Pinwheel Tiling contain an absolutely continuous component?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
The Pinwheel tiling is the non-periodic tiling of the plane introduced by Conway and Radin, generated by an inflation rule on a right triangle with legs 1 and 2, in which tiles appear in infinitely many orientations (a dense set of rotations in SO(2)). To any such tiling T one associates its Dirac comb $\omega_T = \sum_{x \in \Lambda} \delta_x$, where $\Lambda$ is a representative point set (e.g., the set of control points of the tiles). The autocorrelation measure is $\gamma = \lim_{R\to\infty} \frac{1}{|B_R|}\, \omega_T|_{B_R} * \widetilde{\omega_T|_{B_R}}$, and the diffraction measure is $\widehat{\gamma}$, a positive translation-bounded measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$. By the Lebesgue decomposition, $\widehat{\gamma} = \widehat{\gamma}_{pp} + \widehat{\gamma}_{sc} + \widehat{\gamma}_{ac}$, with respect to Lebesgue measure on $\mathbb{R}^2$.

It is known that $\widehat{\gamma}$ is rotation-invariant (circularly symmetric) and that its pure point part is concentrated only at the origin.

Question: Is the absolutely continuous component $\widehat{\gamma}_{ac}$ of the Pinwheel diffraction measure nonzero?
artifact.status_search_result: The status of the absolutely continuous component of the Pinwheel diffraction appears to remain open. The diffraction is known to be circularly symmetric with trivial pure point part (only at the origin) and to contain singular continuous rings; numerical investigations suggest possible additional components, but no rigorous proof of presence or absence of an absolutely continuous part is established in the literature found.

status_evidence.title: Some comments on pinwheel tilings and their diffraction
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of pinwheel diffraction noting sharp rings and possibly a continuous component with circular symmetry; nature of continuous part not fully resolved.
status_evidence.claim: The decomposition of the Pinwheel diffraction beyond the rings (whether absolutely continuous part exists) is not rigorously settled.

status_evidence.title: Pinwheel patterns and powder diffraction
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes circular symmetry of pinwheel diffraction and triviality of pure point part; leaves the precise structure of continuous components open.
status_evidence.claim: Existing rigorous results identify circular symmetry and trivial Bragg part but do not determine the absolutely continuous component.

status_evidence.title: Open problems and conjectures in the theory of mathematical quasicrystals
status_evidence.snippet: Lists as an open problem whether the Pinwheel diffraction has an absolutely continuous component.
status_evidence.claim: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem.
